title: Onboard a new Medical Office Assistant
trigger: A new Medical Office Assistant accepts an offer and a start date is set.
preconditions: Start date confirmed with the clinic manager

roles.name: Clinic Manager
does: signs off the first two weeks

roles.name: Experienced MOA (trainer)
does: walks the new hire through each process
confirms each process was performed once under supervision

roles.name: New hire
does: performs each process once under supervision
uses the process record as the reference, not the trainer

steps.action: Create EMR user account with the correct role template for an MOA; do not copy an existing user's permissions.
Request provincial EHR viewer access and record the request date, because approval takes several days.
Add the new hire to the payroll portal and confirm the first pay period.
Assign one named trainer for the first two weeks. One trainer, not whoever is free.
Walk through booking a new patient appointment, then have the new hire book the next one unassisted.
Walk through referral routing and show both routes (portal and fax) before demonstrating either.
Walk through submitting one insurance claim and reading the rejection queue.
Review the fortnight checklist with the trainer and the new hire; record any process the new hire could not perform unassisted.

decisions.question: How does a referral leave the practice?

branches.when: The receiving specialist accepts portal referrals
branches.then: Send through the provincial portal and confirm the acknowledgement appears.

branches.when: The specialist only accepts fax, or the portal is down
branches.then: Fax the referral and file the transmission confirmation with the referral record.

exceptions.when: Provincial EHR access has not been approved by the start date
exceptions.then: The new hire shadows only; do not share another user's login. Chase the approval daily.

exceptions.when: No trainer is available for the first two weeks
exceptions.then: Move the start date. Starting without a named trainer is how the last two onboarding attempts produced an untrained hire.

outputs: A new hire with working accounts on day one
A fortnight checklist with each process marked performed / not performed
A list of processes the new hire could not complete unassisted, fed back into capture
verification: Clinic Manager confirms each account exists and the role template is correct
New hire performs booking, referral routing and one claim submission unassisted while observed

sources.ref: "Provincial access takes about a week, so request it the day the offer is accepted."
"The mistake we made twice was not naming a trainer."
"Half the specialists take the portal, half only take fax. You have to check."

review.change_note: v2: added the named-trainer requirement after two onboarding attempts without one, and the provincial-access lead time.
